topPRs.title: kona-node-service: support multiple chains in the L1 watcher
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22531.

**Before.** `L1WatcherActor` was built per chain: one rollup config, one derivation client, one unsafe-signer sender and one query receiver, all held flat on the actor. An N-chain host would have needed N watchers, each polling L1 on its own.

**After.** One watcher serves N chains. It holds a `Vec<L1WatcherChain>` and fans every new L1 head and finalized block out to each chain's derivation actor, applies each chain's own system-config address filter, and delivers each chain's unsafe-signer updates to its own network actor. The L1 provider, the two block streams and the L1 head watch stay shared; kona-node builds the same actor with a one-element vec.

**How.** The `select!` arms now only classify the update into a `L1WatcherEvent`; handling happens after the arms' borrows are released, on `L1WatcherChain` methods, which is what lets the query arm hold `&mut` on the chain vec while the head fan-out reads it. Per-chain queries are selected with `futures::future::select_all` over the per-chain receivers, so a closed query channel stays a fatal `StreamEnded` at any N. Logs are fetched per chain (one `eth_getLogs` per chain per head) rather than through one merged multi-address filter, which keeps the single-chain request identical.

---

topPRs.title: op-supernode: gate unsafe sync during invalidation recovery to stop rewind livelock
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Description

Fixes the supernode rewind race / livelock observed on `interop-reorg-2` (2026-07-21, ~21:14–21:56 UTC), where the same invalid Chain B block `515624` was invalidated repeatedly, each cycle freezing and resetting the VNs of **both** chains and walking local-safe back a full sequencing window (~40k blocks, safe-head sawtooth).

### Root cause

The deny list is only enforced on the derivation path (`onPayloadProcess` → deposits-only replacement) and the sequencer build path. **Unsafe ingestion — the clsync queue and the driver gap-fill (`checkForGapInUnsafeQueue`) — never consults it.** After an invalidation rewind + deposits-only replacement:

1. Gossip keeps delivering the sequencer's far-ahead unsafe tip, which descends from the *original* (denied, EVM-valid) block.
2. The gap-fill force-inserts that far-ahead payload; `NewPayload` returns `SYNCING` (tolerated in CLSync precisely to trigger EL sync), and the follow-up FCU points the EL at the denied branch.
3. The EL backfills and canonicalizes the denied ancestry — undoing the replacement — while interim `SYNCING` FCU responses trigger `ResetError` → `FindL2Heads` → sequencing-window-deep local-safe walkback on every chain.
4. The verifier's frontier re-observes the same invalid executing message on the re-canonicalized block → same invalidation → loop.

## Commits

**1. `op-acceptance-tests: repro supernode re-adoption of an invalidated block`** — the failing repro (red). `TestSupernodeDoesNotReadoptInvalidatedBlock` (light-sequencer preset): invalid exec message on chain B, sequencer builds ~20 blocks ahead on the invalid branch, supernode invalidates and replaces, then a far-ahead descendant of the invalid block is delivered over unsafe sync. Asserts verification durably passes the replacement while the invalid block is never re-adopted as canonical. Includes two infra fixes required for the repro to be meaningful: the supernode VN factory now honors persisted sequencer state (`cfg.LoadPersisted`) and the devstack VN config uses real config persistence — previously a VN restart mid-invalidation silently resurrected the bootstrap sequencer (dual-sequencing with the light CL) and self-healed the chain, masking the bug. New DSL: `L2ELNode.AwaitBlockReplaced`, `Supernode.AwaitValidatedTimestampWithoutReadoption`.

**2. `op-supernode: drop unsafe payloads during invalidation recovery`** — the fix (green). Unsafe ingestion is gated while the highest denied height is above the finalized head — from the moment of an invalidation until finality passes it. Gated payloads are refused at **queue entry** (`AddUnsafePayload`, so none survive the window to be gap-filled after it closes) and at **insert** (`insertUnsafePayload`, covering the ELSync direct path). During the window the chain advances via (deny-list-checked) derivation only. Finality is the earliest provably-safe exit: while the denied branch can still be canonicalized, a far-ahead FCU would push the EL into a sync ending in an inconsistent forkchoice and another reset. Outside the window the cost is one local deny-list read per insert and unsafe sync behaves byte-for-byte stock; plain op-nodes (nil `SuperAuthority`) are unaffected. Plumbing: `SuperAuthority.MaxDeniedHeight()` backed by a bbolt `Cursor().Last()` read on the supernode `DenyList`.

**3. `op-supernode: enrich invalidation logs with rewind target`** — observability. The invalidation logs now name blocks by role — `invalidatedBlock` and `rewindToValidParent`, each a full `hash:number` pair — plus the decision timestamp, so operators can see exactly which block was reorged out and which valid block the chain must roll back to. Also logs pruned deny-list entries when an L1 reorg removes their decision basis (previously silent).

**4. `op-devstack: fix goimports formatting in supernode runtime`** — formatting only (fixes `go-lint`).

**5. `op-supernode: document sequencing disabled after invalidation rewind`** — comment-only. The rewind restarts every VN (invalidated chain and frozen peers alike) through op-node's graceful shutdown, which persists `sequencer.stopped=true`; with commit 1's persistence fix the restarted VNs honor that state. A supernode that was actively sequencing therefore exits invalidation recovery with sequencing disabled on **all** chains until an explicit operator/conductor `admin_startSequencer` — intentional: operator stops survive restarts, and internal restarts must not silently resurrect a sequencer (that resurrection was the bug-masking behavior commit 1 removed).

**6. `op-acceptance-tests: re-enable sequencing after invalidation rewind`** — the virtual-sequencer tests play the operator: after the reset is detected they re-enable sequencing on both chains via admin RPC. The helper is guarded by `SequencerActive`, so light-sequencer topologies (whose sequencing CLs never restart) are untouched. No assertions were added, removed, or weakened.

**7. `op-devstack: sequence light CLs from genesis with CLSync`** — harness fix. An ELSync CL cannot produce block 1: it only leaves `willStartEL` on the first network payload, which as sole sequencer it is itself supposed to produce (#21164). Light sequencer CLs now boot with CLSync when sequencing from genesis; VN-bootstrap mode keeps ELSync for the pre-handoff sync from the VN, so the `follow_l2` bootstrap tests are unaffected (validated locally).

**8. `op-acceptance-tests: start light sequencers from genesis`** — the light invalid-message and readoption tests drop the VN-sequencer bootstrap + handoff entirely: light CLs sequence from genesis with the batcher following them, matching production wiring (batchers point at the light sequencer nodes, not the supernode). This also removes a recovery livelock latent in the old bootstrap wiring: a batcher pinned to the supernode VN starves during invalidation recovery — unsafe deny gating freezes the VN's view, so no new batches reach L1 and finality can never pass the denied height to end the gating window.

### Operational notes

- During the recovery window (~an L1 finality delay) VN unsafe heads intentionally sit at the replacement block and advance at derivation speed, even if the sequencer heals instantly.
- After recovery, sequencing is disabled on every chain in the supernode (see commit 5). Deployments where the supernode is the active sequencer need an operator or conductor-like automation to re-enable it, same as a restarted production sequencer op-node.

### Found along the way (follow-up, not fixed here)

While validating the fix, the acceptance test exposed that **op-reth applies the forkchoice head update before validating safe/finalized ancestry**: an FCU whose head descends from the denied branch was canonicalized (reorging below finalized) before reth returned the inconsistent-forkchoice error. Engine API spec says such an FCU must be rejected without side effects. The queue-entry gate in this PR prevents the supernode from ever issuing that FCU, but the EL behavior deserves its own fix.

### Tests

- Acceptance (devstack): red/green repro as above; plus the pre-existing invalidation suite validated locally and in CI against the final stack — `TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`, `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`, `TestSupernodeInteropRPCGatedDuringReorg`, `TestSupernodeResyncSchedulesAtActivation_PreActivation`, `TestSupernodeDoesNotReadoptInvalidatedBlock`.
- Engine controller units: payloads dropped at queue entry and insert during recovery (contiguous + gap); stock behavior with an empty deny list; stock behavior restored once finality passes the denied height; nil-authority path unchanged.
- `DenyList.MaxDeniedHeight` across add/prune.

### Metadata

- Incident write-up: Notion "Supernode Rewind Race Condition" (interop-reorg-2, 2026-07-21)

topPRs.title: kona-gossip: Allowlist gossip subscription topics
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Kona built the gossipsub behaviour with `libp2p::gossipsub::Behaviour::new`, which takes the default `AllowAllSubscriptionFilter`. libp2p therefore accepted a subscription for any topic a peer announced, and emitted an `Event::Subscribed` for it.

A connected peer could abuse this in two ways:

- It grew its `PeerDetails.topics` set in the swarm peer table. That set has no cap. The memory is freed only when the peer disconnects.
- It minted an unbounded number of `topic` label values on the `kona_node_gossip_events` gauge. Kona builds the Prometheus recorder with no idle timeout, so those series never expire. They outlive the connection and grow the scrape response for the life of the process.

This is an availability problem, not a correctness one. Gossipsub already drops messages on topics we do not subscribe to, so block validation was never affected.

This change installs a `WhitelistSubscriptionFilter` built from the topics the handlers serve. The same predicate gates our own subscriptions and inbound announcements, so the whitelist cannot drift from the subscribed set.

op-node has carried the same allowlist since `BuildSubscriptionFilter` was added, for the same stated reason. Neither node conditions the topic set on scheduled forks: op-node allowlists and subscribes to all four block topics unconditionally, and gates forks only at publish time and in the per-topic validators. Kona's `BlockHandler::topics()` already matches that, so all four stay allowed at all times.

The `gossipsub` field gains type parameters. A new public `Gossipsub` alias keeps consumers from spelling them.

Found while reviewing #22569. That PR could not pre-create the `topic` label values in `zero()` because the set was unbounded. With this filter the set is bounded at four, so a follow-up can pre-create them.

Reviews run: `rust-code-reviewer` (no blocking findings; three suggestions applied — type alias, positive-case assertion, assertion messages). Two suggestions dismissed: a direct unit test on `filter_incoming_subscriptions` needs `libp2p::gossipsub::Subscription`, which the crate does not export; a comment about the empty-handler case is unnecessary because the builder always passes one handler.
